title: Split SRP: a Talker Advertise replacing a Talker Failed waits for the old registration to leave
body:
Part of #665 (Mark II split flip). Found by the in-house replica on the test machine (#665 issuecomment-6904803181, finding 18). The release passed the same scenario on Oct 31.

**Defect.** When a talker replaces its Talker Failed with a Talker Advertise, the DUT's Listener stays Asking Failed until the old Talker Failed registration leaves (2.1 s on the bench, at the talker's next MRPDU); every other transition in the feature took 0.6 to 0.9 s, and the scenario wants Ready within 1 s. In `sw/firmware/ctrl/srp/srp_mbx.c` a registered Talker Failed sets the sink's desired state to Asking Failed, and a Talker Advertise sets Ready only when the desired state is not Asking Failed, so a still-registered Talker Failed outranks the newer Talker Advertise. IEEE 802.1Q-2018 35.2.4: a talker declares one of the two attributes for a stream.

**Scope.** The most recently registered of Talker Advertise and Talker Failed decides the Listener declaration (or a Talker Advertise's New replaces the Talker Failed); firmware unit tests and the lwSRP receive tests, with planted defects caught by name; the SRP campaign and the service-budget rows within bound.

**Acceptance.** All gates rc 0 on the final head; on the bench, the scenario reaches Listener Ready within 1 s of the Talker Advertise.
